source.title: Siamese labels auxiliary learning
source.authors: Wen-Rui Gan; Zhu-Lin Liu; C. L. Philip Chen; Tong Zhang

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the paper through its references; some figure labels are garbled, and several tables are flattened.
record.tranche_reason: Reports its own results on held-out classification performance and a training-loss perturbation measure, using methods and measures not specified in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out accuracy comparisons for SiLa and dynamic SiLa, plus training NLL changes after Gaussian parameter noise. These results do not measure the random-label/natural-label comparison, interpolation-threshold widening, convolutional versus fully connected gap, optimizer or batch-size gap, dropout effects, a training–test gap linked to magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates its own auxiliary training method and uses parameter robustness to interpret its performance. None of its comparisons tests V1–V8. In particular, Figure 7b measures training-NLL sensitivity to Gaussian parameter noise without magnitude scaling or an analysis of training–test gaps, so it does not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that SiLa improves classification without increasing test parameters, combines with DML, and improves early-exit networks at the same computing budget. They interpret reduced sensitivity to parameter noise as evidence of more robust parameters and improved generalization; this interpretation does not establish V7.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Siamese-label auxiliary training and dynamic early-exit networks; evaluates held-out accuracy and training-loss changes under Gaussian parameter noise, rather than the interventions or gap measures in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and task differ across the reported dynamic-network evaluations; compute budget varies in Figures 4 and 5.

fits_no_version.finding: SiLa improves reported test accuracy over original MSDNet at matched block counts and computing budgets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Siamese-label auxiliary training can improve early-exit image-classification accuracy without increasing inference parameters.

fits_no_version.finding: SiLa-trained ResNet18 models show smaller training-NLL increases under Gaussian parameter noise than independently trained models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Siamese-label auxiliary training can reduce training-loss sensitivity to Gaussian parameter perturbations on CIFAR-100.

record.problems: Several numerical tables are flattened, and the relevant Gaussian-noise and dynamic-network comparisons are presented in figures without exact values in the text. The paper does not report uncertainty for these comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 1–3 report numerous model-specific accuracy values, but the supplied flattened layout does not support reliable assignment of all values to model, method, and metric. Figure 6 gives a visual MNIST example, but the text says that experiment focuses on visualization rather than classification accuracy. Figure 7a's training NLL curves are not extracted because the stated near-zero convergence and higher SiLa NLL do not give a numerical held-out result.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Test-error changes as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and interventions on local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes to the training recipe.
Dropout effects and their dependence on training-set size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus training–test gaps, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Differences in dataset-specific batch sizes or network architectures are not controlled tests of batch size or architectural bias. The additional accuracy tables and MNIST visualization do not supply results on any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance versus natural-label performance.
Width sweep past interpolation and test-error trajectory.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local-connectivity interventions.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out comparisons and tuning conditions.
Large-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout addition/removal and its interaction with training-set size or augmentation.
Does not measure a training–test gap or test magnitude-aware sharpness against that gap. Gaussian-noise changes in training NLL are not that measure.
Does not remove memorized examples or measure resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: SiLa (block=5) and MSDNet (block=5)
rows.operation_detail: Trained dynamic neural networks with SiLa or the original MSDNet, then compared test accuracy at matched MSD-block counts.

conditions.value: Anytime Prediction and Budgeted Batch Classification
SGD; CIFAR-100 300 epochs, batch size 64; ImageNet-100 90 epochs, batch size 256

rows.measure: Top-1 test accuracy as a function of compute budget
rows.note: Authors state that SiLa performs better than original MSDNet at the same number of MSD-blocks and compute resources. Figures provide the plotted comparisons; exact values are not stated in text.
rows.check: This is the study's own method compared with MSDNet, not a result on any claim version. The reported accuracy improvement cannot establish a version's effect. The row also combines two datasets and two tasks; Figures 4–5 additionally include seven-block networks on CIFAR-100.

rows.subject: ResNet18 trained with SiLa and independently trained ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Measured training NLL change after adding Gaussian noise to model parameters.

conditions.value: Training NLL change after Gaussian parameter noise
standard deviation σ; exact value not stated

rows.measure: Change in training NLL after Gaussian parameter noise
rows.note: Text says SiLa and DML both have smaller NLL changes than Independent; no exact values are stated. This is a training-loss perturbation result, not a measured training–test gap.
rows.check: Smaller training-NLL changes under Gaussian parameter noise are reported, but do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization-gap relationship. The original partial state is therefore inappropriate. Figure 7b varies noise standard deviation rather than reporting one unspecified noise level.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
